# Summary

In this study, we analyzed data within residents and directors, then compared the groups' answer selections, informing the difference that various factors can have on a resident's wellbeing and experience in their program, and if the directors have a different perception of what residents face during residency. Out of 81 tests within the residents group, we found 7 to be significant, but because of the amount of tests, zero were significant after adjusting for the false discovery rate. Out of 14 tests for directors, we found 0 to be true both before and after adjustment. We had a total of 119 residents and 24 directors in our data, which for some questions with many categorical responses, made it difficult to find significance. However, when cross-comparing the groups on each common question, we found 20/51 comparisons to be significant, 18 after adjustment. This means that at least 18 questions saw significant evidence of being answered differently for residents and directors. All significant tests will be reported in the results section, and their significance before and after adjustment will be noted.

# Methods

For our methodology, we conducted Fisher exact tests, which can calculate exact probabilities to see if there's a non-random association between groups. A low p-value (after adjustment) translates to having significant evidence for there existing some association between questions.

For questions that had multiple parts, we had to split them into individual questions (e.g. 8a, 8b, 8c...) to see if there were specific responses that were influenced by the grouping variable in question, which was the role (being a resident/director) in the case of cross-comparison, or information like program, experience, etc. In practice, this saw us, for example, analyzing whether directors think residents should be comfortable recognizing oral soft-tissue changes related to cigarettes, ENDS/vaping, and so on, for each part. Each sub-question statistically needs to be considered independently, which is why they are separated in the analysis.

Then, to visualize the difference, we created side-by-side bar charts which plot the distribution of question responses versus the grouping variable. For resident/director comparison, this shows side-by-side plots of the residents' response to a question versus the directors'. Noticeable/interesting plots and findings were placed in the "significant findings" section of this writeup and all plots, significant or not, are in the appendix.

# 

Below are several tables outlining each of the categories of analysis requested.

```{r, echo = FALSE}
validation <- function(question1, question2, data){
  df <- data %>%
    transmute(
      response1 = .data[[question1]],
      response2 = .data[[question2]]
    ) %>%
    drop_na()
  
  comparison_res <- df %>%
    group_by(response1, response2) %>%
    summarize(counts = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    group_by(response2) %>%
    mutate(percent = counts / sum(counts) * 100) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  table_comparison <- table(df$response2, df$response1)
  #table_hours
  test <- suppressWarnings(chisq.test(table_comparison))
  
  if (mean(test$expected <= 5) < 0.8 | any(test$expected < 1)){
    fish_test <- fisher.test(table_comparison, simulate.p.value = TRUE)
    if (fish_test$p.value <= 0.05){
      significant <- TRUE
    }
    else {
      significant <- FALSE
    }
    return(c("question1", "question2", round(fish_test$p.value, digits = 4), significant, "fisher"))
  }
  else{
    if (test$p.value <= 0.05){
      significant <- TRUE
    }
    else {
      significant <- FALSE
    }
  }
  return(c("question1", "question2", round(test$p.value, digits = 4), significant, "chisq"))
}
```

## Resident/Dentist Comfort & Clinical Practice Analysis

Below is a table comparing residents and dentists comfort levels and clinical practices.

```{r, echo = FALSE}
comfort_dic <- data.frame(
  q_ref = c("Q8a",  "Q8b",  "Q8c",  "Q8d",  "Q8e",  "Q8f", "Q8g",  "Q8h" , "Q8i" , "Q8j" , "Q8k" , "Q9" ,  "Q10a" ,"Q10b", "Q11a" ,"Q11b"), 
  role = c(rep("role", 16))
)

comfort_results <- data.frame(
  Question1 = character(),
  Question2 = character(),
  P_value = numeric(),
  Significant = logical(), 
  Test = character()
)

for (i in seq_len(nrow(comfort_dic))) {
  
  comfort_results[i, ] <- validation(
    question1 = comfort_dic$q_ref[i],
    question2 = comfort_dic$role[i],
    data = m_coalesced
  )
}

comfort_results <- comfort_results %>%
  mutate(
    Adj_P = round(p.adjust(P_value, method = "BH"), digits = 4),
    Sig_Adj = Adj_P <= 0.05,
    Question1 = comfort_dic$q_ref, 
    Question2 = comfort_dic$role
  ) %>% 
  arrange(Adj_P)

comfort_results
```

# Appendix A: Plots 

```{r, echo = F}
stack_bar <- function(q_reference, q_group, data){
  bar_df <- data %>%
    group_by(.data[[q_reference]], .data[[q_group]]) %>%
    summarize(counts = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    drop_na() %>%
    group_by(.data[[q_group]]) %>%
    mutate(percent = counts / sum(counts) * 100) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  p <- ggplot(bar_df, aes(x = .data[[q_reference]], y = percent, fill = .data[[q_reference]])) +
    geom_col() +
    facet_wrap(vars(.data[[q_group]])) +
    labs(
      title = paste(q_reference, "vs", q_group, sep = " "),
      x = NULL,
      y = "Percent of responses"
    ) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.x = element_blank()
    )
  return(p)
}
```

## Comfort & Clinical Practice Plots

Below are plots comparing the comfort and clinical practices between residents and dentists.

```{r, echo = F}
plots_comfort <- pmap(comfort_dic, 
                   function(q_ref, role){
                     stack_bar(
                       q_reference = q_ref, 
                       q_group = role,
                       data = m_coalesced
                     )
                   })
walk(plots_comfort, print)
```
